thread:
support-jen: FYI: Customer alex@example.com reporting repeated 503s from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. They see upstream worker exits and acks from the gateway. Escalating — can SRE triage?

support-jen: Short logs attached by customer: `GET /v1/generate -> 503` then `upstream exit code 139` and container restarted.

customer-alex: Seeing this in prod for our v2/chat model. Happens ~1/20 requests, mostly at higher seq lengths. No auth change on our side. Token: redacted.

deploy-bot: [alert] hosted-infer-cluster-prod: worker-eviction spike detected (09:11:42 UTC), 5 restarts in 3m on pool gpu-pool-a.

sre-eli: Thanks Jen — assigning. Any recent deploys to hosted runtime?

eng-runtime-liu: No full runtime push in the last 48h. We did push a quant-micropatch to model-variants last week but not to runtime.

sre-eli: Can you paste the worker logs around the crash? Need tail of stderr and any CUDA errors. Also what GPU/driver?

support-jen: pasted what customer provided:

```
[2026-03-17T09:10:17Z] infer-runner[pid=4123]: INFO processing request id=ck_... seq_len=2048 batch=1
[2026-03-17T09:10:19Z] infer-runner[pid=4123]: ERROR cuda failure: out of memory while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-17T09:10:19Z] infer-runner[pid=4123]: fatal: signal 11 (segfault) at 0x7f8b... -- dumping core
[2026-03-17T09:10:20Z] docker[container=runner-4123]: INFO container exit status=139
```

support-jen: Customer says seq_len spike correlates with failures, they send batches with long prompts.

prodops-sam: That allocation size (2GB) is suspicious but plausible for logits+KV with long sequences. We need to know if prefetch/KV cache is enabled for that route.

eng-runtime-liu: On prod routes we enable kv-prefetch by default. There's a new cache eviction change from two days ago — could be interaction with memory accounting. I'll pull the runtime metrics.

sre-eli: Workaround options we can push now: 1) route traffic for that customer to fallback model variant with lower memory profile, 2) enforce per-request max_seq_len via gateway for that API key, 3) temporarily increase pool size or enable burst nodes. Which should we try fastest?

support-jen: Customer prefers minimal changes to prompts. They asked for a fast fix on our side — routing them to fallback is acceptable.

prodops-sam: I'll add a temporary route rule to send their API key to model-quant-128 variant (lower KV memory). Patching now.

deploy-bot: [action] route-rule updated: api_key=ck_... -> model=model-quant-128, applied by prodops-sam at 09:14:55 UTC.

customer-alex: Confirmed — requests now succeed (200) for a few tests. Still seeing slower tail latency but no 503s so far. Thanks.

sre-eli: Good. Now for root cause: Liu, can you pull GPU OOM counts, nvml logs, and the runtime heap usage for the failing container ids? Also collect core dump.

eng-runtime-liu: Pulling metrics now. Preliminary: pool gpu-pool-a had 3 OOMs in 10m window. nvml shows a GPU reset on index 0 at 09:10:19 with `GPU reset required` and subsequent container kill. Core dump uploaded to s3://redwood-infer/coredumps/2977770000/runner-4123.core (perm restricted).

sre-eli: Thanks. Hypothesis: long sequences + kv-prefetch + minor accounting bug cause allocation overshoot -> cuda OOM -> segfault. Follow-ups: a) add stricter guardrail in gateway to reject requests with seq_len > 2048 for vulnerable pools, b) runtime fix to account for prefetch memory in alloc headroom, c) add better autoscale to spin burst nodes earlier.

eng-runtime-liu: I'll open a runbook PR for the runtime accounting fix and a changelist to include a safety margin of 10% when computing allocation. Target: canary next week.

prodops-sam: In the short term I've propagated a per-key seq_len cap of 2048 and increased pool autoscale aggressiveness (scale-up grace 30s -> 15s) for gpu-pool-a.

support-jen: Notifying customer of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. Will keep thread updated.

customer-alex: Appreciate the quick routing workaround. Please keep me posted on permanent fix timeline — we need to support long chats.

sre-eli: Thanks all. Actions tracked: 1) route fallback applied (done), 2) gate seq_len per-key (done), 3) collect & analyze core dump (eng-runtime-liu), 4) runtime accounting change (eng-runtime-liu, PR opened), 5) monitor for recurrence and rollback route if stable. I'll re-open if more 503s after rollback. :white_check_mark:
